facts.authoredFrom: Read from the case's input bytes: grund.toml (version 1, project_name "fixture", strict, `require_grounding = false`, `[id] format = "{kind}-{slug}"`, one untitled FS kind on the folder docs/fs with `index = false`, and no `[scan]` table, so the default include reads docs and src with the default extensions and the default comment prefixes, `/*` among them, §FS-config.3.5); the FS home docs/fs does not exist and scans as nothing with no finding (§FS-scan.scope.homes); src/lib.rs is one `/*! … */` block: its opener line 1 `/*! FS-b: Beta` is in declaration position behind the `/*!` opener, a form the configured `/*` stands for (§FS-declarations.line.block-comment, §FS-languages.prefixes.forms), so it declares FS-b titled Beta at line 1 with a null anchor (§FS-show.3.1.3.1). The block runs from that opener to the `*/` on line 4 (§FS-languages.comment-block.close); its body is lines 2-3, the blank line and the bare `Beta body.` kept as written, while the closer alone on line 4 is dropped (§FS-languages.comment-wrapper), so the body reads `Beta body.` and there is no section. `list` gives the one catalog line `FS-b  src/lib.rs:1  Beta` (§FS-list.2). docs/use.md carries one line, `See §FS-b.`, a marked citation under no heading, so outside any declaration; it resolves to the source declaration, which is therefore cited. Every citation resolves and the one declaration is cited, so the only finding is the site-less version caution (§FS-check.2.1.1). Cross-reference emission wraps that citation as a link to src/lib.rs, relative to docs/, with no anchor because the target's home is a source file (§FS-fmt.6.2, §FS-show.3.1.3.1); the Rust file is not Markdown and is never rewritten (§FS-fmt.6.1). FS-absent is the absent control, an ID of the config's format that nothing declares or cites.

findings.message: grund.toml is version 1; migrate it with grund config migrate --to 2
